blogs.title: Imaging the Mystery Masses: How Ultrasound and Non‑Contrast MRI Unmask Pedunculated Leiomyomas in Pregnancy
blogs.description: A deep dive into the imaging work‑up of large intra‑abdominal masses detected in the second trimester. We’ll review sonographic hallmarks that separate pedunculated or cystically degenerated leiomyomas from decidualized endometriomas, explore Doppler patterns of vascularity, and outline safe non‑contrast MRI protocols (field strength limits, sequences) that enhance diagnostic confidence without compromising fetal safety. Practical pearls include a stepwise algorithm for radiologists and obstetricians faced with atypical mass morphology.

blogs.title: The CA‑125 Puzzle: Decoding Tumor Marker Elevation Amidst Mid‑Trimester Physiology
blogs.description: CA‑125 rises physiologically early in pregnancy but can also signal ovarian pathology or uterine leiomyoma activity. This post examines normal gestational reference ranges, trimester‑specific peaks, and how to interpret modest elevations (e.g., >35 U/mL) in a woman over 40 years old. We’ll discuss the utility of serial trending versus single measurements, compare other markers (CEA, CA 19‑9), and propose an evidence‑based pathway for integrating tumor marker data into the differential diagnosis of pelvic masses during pregnancy.

blogs.title: Surgery or Watchful Waiting? Decision Framework for Myomectomy During the Second Trimester
blogs.description: When does a symptomatic leiomyoma mandate operative intervention? Drawing from this case and recent obstetric literature, we present a structured decision matrix that weighs symptom severity (pain, dyspnoea), complication risk (torsion, necrosis, infection), gestational age, mass size/location, and obstetric implications. The article outlines thresholds for proceeding to surgery versus expectant management and highlights multidisciplinary consent processes that balance maternal health with fetal preservation.

blogs.title: Open Laparotomy Versus Laparoscopy for Pregnant Myomas: Choosing the Right Approach When Size Matters
blogs.description: Large or multiple myomas present a technical crossroads—open laparotomy or minimally invasive laparoscopy? This entry reviews current guidelines on surgical access during pregnancy, compares peri‑operative outcomes (blood loss, operative time, preterm labor rates), discusses patient selection criteria (mass >8 cm, intramural location, gestational age >20 weeks), and offers practical tips for safe laparoscopic entry (Hasson technique) when feasible. Real‑world data from series on cesarean plus myomectomy will be incorporated.

blogs.title: Safeguarding Mother and Baby: Anesthetic Strategies, Progesterone Prophylaxis, and Peri‑Operative Care in In‑Pregnancy Abdominal Surgery
blogs.description: A comprehensive guide to peri‑operative management of pregnant patients undergoing abdominal operations. Topics include fetal heart rate monitoring before/during/after surgery per Zhao et al., choice of anesthetic agents compatible with uteroplacental perfusion, use of intra‑operative progesterone supplementation to reduce miscarriage risk—reviewing limited evidence—and tailored antibiotic regimens addressing concurrent urinary infection. The post also addresses anemia correction strategies (IV iron versus transfusion thresholds) specific to the pregnant physiologic state.

blogs.title: From Myomectomy to Cesarean Delivery: Planning Birth After Intra‑Pregnancy Uterine Surgery
blogs.description: How does an intra‑pregnancy myomectomy shape delivery planning? This article explores indications for elective cesarean section after uterine surgery—including residual posterior pelvic fibroids that hinder fetal head descent—risk assessment for uterine scar rupture versus trial of labor after myomectomy (TOLAM), timing of delivery at ≥37 weeks, and counseling about postoperative leiomyoma regression. Long‑term follow up strategies—including imaging surveillance and criteria for delayed definitive myomectomy postpartum—are also discussed.
